findings.title: Failed device-limit check poisons the local cache and lets the device in on retry
findings.body: tagDeviceUI writes the device key to localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and never removes it when that call fails. A new device over the limit is denied on its first request, but the cache entry remains for the 29-minute cache TTL; on its next request tagDeviceUI returns nil on the cache hit without touching the store, TagDevice returns nil, and Anonymous.Authenticate grants an identity. The configured limit is therefore bypassed after a single denied attempt on the same instance. Set the cache entry only after a successful store write, or delete it when CreateOrUpdateDevice returns an error.

findings.title: Device limit is enforced by a non-atomic count-then-insert and can be exceeded concurrently
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice runs CountDevices in one DB session and, if the count is below the limit, performs the INSERT/UPSERT in a separate session with no transaction, lock, or other serialization. Concurrent first-time requests for distinct devices (across goroutines or Grafana instances sharing the database) can all observe count == limit-1 and all insert, exceeding the configured limit. The check-and-create needs to be atomic, e.g. inside a transaction with appropriate locking.

findings.title: Provider signature changes are not reflected in wire generation, breaking the server build
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now takes db.DB instead of anonstore.AnonStore and constructs the store itself, and ProvideAnonDBStore now takes an int64 deviceLimit that wire cannot supply. The checked-in pkg/server/wire_gen.go is not updated in this PR and still calls both providers with their old signatures, so the server package will not compile; the wire provider set also still needs to drop/replace ProvideAnonDBStore and be regenerated.

findings.title: Anonymous authentication now blocks on the database with no timeout or panic isolation
findings.body: Authenticate previously tagged the device in a goroutine with a 2-minute background-context timeout and panic recovery; it now calls TagDevice synchronously with the request context and no deadline. A slow or stalled device-store query (count plus upsert, now on the auth path) blocks anonymous authentication indefinitely, a client disconnect cancels the tagging via the request context, and a panic in tagging now propagates into authentication. Keep the synchronous enforcement needed for the limit, but bound it with a timeout context and recover from panics.

findings.title: updateDevice can falsely report the limit reached for an existing MySQL device
findings.body: updateDevice treats RowsAffected == 0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL, RowsAffected for UPDATE counts changed rows, not matched rows; when an already-known device is re-tagged (e.g. via another instance whose local cache is cold) within the same second and with unchanged client_ip/user_agent, the stored updated_at has second precision so nothing changes and MySQL reports 0. A legitimate, already-counted device is then denied as if it were new. Use a matched-row check (existence SELECT, or found-rows semantics) instead of relying on changed-row counts.

findings.title: No test covers an existing device updating successfully while at the limit, or client-level denial
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only verifies that a second, new device is rejected when the limit is 1. The other half of the feature branch—an already-registered device calling CreateOrUpdateDevice again while count >= limit must succeed via updateDevice—is untested, as is Anonymous.Authenticate returning an error (and no identity) on ErrDeviceLimitReached and unlimited behavior with limit 0 end to end (impl_test.go always uses a default cfg with limit 0). A regression in updateDevice would ship undetected.

findings.title: New device_limit option is not added to default configuration or documentation
findings.body: The PR reads [auth.anonymous] device_limit into Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit but does not add it to conf/defaults.ini (or the configuration documentation). Operators have no discoverable way to learn the option exists or that 0 means unlimited and negative values are also treated as unlimited by the deviceLimit > 0 guard. Add the setting with its default and semantics to defaults.ini and the auth.anonymous docs.
